verdicts.quote: the schedule shown and saved is: 3 days before the due date, on the due date, 7 days after, 14 days after, until the owner edits it.

No reminder is sent for an invoice that is in any of these states: draft (not yet issued), paid in full, void or cancelled, written off or marked uncollectible, or reduced to a zero balance by credits or refunds.
verdicts.missing: Whether a disputed invoice or one on a payment plan stops the sequence; neither state is mentioned (part-paid is decided in C-18, pending payments in C-19).

verdicts.quote: After a partial payment, later reminders for that invoice are sent and state the remaining balance, not the original total.
the customer receives at most one email in total, including when two workers evaluate the same step simultaneously, when a worker restarts partway through, and when the scheduler runs twice.

If the invoice stopped being eligible (C-17, C-19), was paused (C-33), or the account setting was turned off after the step became due but before the email was handed to the email provider, no email is sent
the attempt is retried 1 hour later, up to 3 retries (4 attempts in all); if the fourth also fails the step shows "failed".
verdicts.missing: Whether anyone is notified or escalated to when sending keeps failing; the spec only marks the step failed in the history (C-45).

verdicts.quote: When the provider answers that the account is being rate-limited, the step is retried under C-25 and not marked failed on the first answer.
verdicts.missing: How a large batch is paced to stay within the provider's rate limit; the spec only reacts to throttle answers and states a 10,000-in-60-minutes target (C-16).

verdicts.quote: every unsent step of an affected invoice whose scheduled time is already past at that moment shows "skipped: before start" and is never sent later... The triggers are: the owner turns reminders on
Reminders go out at 09:00 in the account's time zone, or in UTC if the account has no time zone
verdicts.missing: The customer's local time zone, and whether weekends and holidays are avoided; only the account's time zone and a fixed 09:00 are decided.

verdicts.quote: The amount is the remaining balance at the time of sending (C-18), with its currency, to the currency's usual number of decimal places. The due date is shown in a form that cannot be misread

When the invoice has no billing email address, or the address is not a syntactically valid email address, the step shows "skipped: no recipient"... When the provider reports a permanent delivery failure (hard bounce), the step shows "bounced"
The email's recipient is exactly the invoice's billing contact email address as it stands when the attempt is made... No other person is copied or blind-copied.

For each step of the schedule the owner sees its offset, scheduled date, and one outcome: upcoming, sent, skipped (with reason), cancelled (with reason), failed, unconfirmed, or bounced, and the time the outcome was recorded
the invoice number, the amount still owed, the due date... a way to pay or view the invoice... The link still works on the day of the last scheduled reminder and any day the invoice remains unpaid.
Only users permitted to manage billing settings can change reminder settings or pause and resume an invoice's reminders
verdicts.missing: Who may send a reminder by hand; manual sending is not defined at all.

verdicts.quote: A single account-level setting shows "on" or "off" and changes when saved
verdicts.missing: Turning reminders off per customer (only per invoice via C-33), any preview or dry-run, and resending a reminder by hand.

verdicts.quote: its offset, scheduled date, and one outcome: upcoming, sent... failed, unconfirmed, or bounced... a step in the states failed, unconfirmed or bounced is marked differently from a sent step so it can be found at a glance.
When the system first handles a due step and its scheduled time is more than 24 hours ago (for example after the scheduler was down), no email is sent and the step shows "skipped: missed".
Issuing, editing, paying, voiding and writing off invoices, and the emails the system already sends about invoices, behave and look exactly as before the release, whether reminders are on or off.
